keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «사람들이 모두가 가치 있다고 인정한 물건을 돈으로 쓰기 시작했다(해결)» 와 «돈은 언제나 믿음 위에 세워져 있다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the solution (people began using objects that everyone agreed were valuable) and the conclusion (money has always been built on trust). The green sentences are the answers.

words: people traded things they had for things they needed
gave one thing to get another thing
to take something that is offered

believing that someone or something is honest and reliable

qs.q: Why can a number on a screen work as money?
qs.qko: 화면 속 숫자가 돈으로 쓰일 수 있는 까닭은 무엇인가요?
opts: Because millions of people trust that others will accept it
Because the number is made of gold
Because banks print it on paper
evs: It works only because millions of people trust that others will accept it.
Most money is no longer shells, coins, or paper, but just numbers stored on bank computers.
In parts of Africa and Asia, small shells called cowries became money.
The clerk would probably laugh, but long ago, this was how people shopped.
why: 화면 속 숫자는 그 자체로는 가치가 없지만, 수많은 사람이 다른 사람도 그것을 받아 줄 거라고 믿기 때문에 돈으로 쓰인다고 했어요.
A number has no value by itself, but it works because millions of people trust that others will accept it.

qs.q: In "The clerk would probably laugh," what does "clerk" mean?
qs.qko: «The clerk would probably laugh» 에서 «clerk» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: a person who works in a store
evs: Imagine walking into a store and trying to pay for a snack with a live chicken.
To solve this, people began using objects that everyone agreed were valuable.
Most money is no longer shells, coins, or paper, but just numbers stored on bank computers.
A number on a screen has no value by itself.
why: 바로 앞에서 가게에 들어가 과자값을 내려는 장면이 나와요. 그러니 «clerk» 는 가게에서 일하는 «점원» 이에요.
You walk into a store to pay for a snack, so a «clerk» is a person who works in a store.

qs.q: Which two things were used as money before paper money and bank numbers?
qs.qko: 지폐와 숫자 돈이 나오기 전에 돈으로 쓰인 두 가지는 무엇인가요?
opts: Small shells called cowries and metal coins
evs: In parts of Africa and Asia, small shells called cowries became money.
Before money existed, people traded things they had for things they needed.
About 2,600 years ago, some of the first metal coins appeared in a kingdom in what is now Turkey, and China later became one of the first places to use paper money.
A number on a screen has no value by itself.
why: 아프리카와 아시아에서는 카우리라는 작은 조개껍데기가 돈이 되었고, 약 2,600년 전에는 금속 동전이 나타났다고 했어요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
Small shells called cowries became money, and about 2,600 years ago metal coins appeared. You need both sentences.

ends: Why do countries put famous people on their money?
왜 나라마다 지폐에 유명한 인물을 넣을까요?
How can we spend and save money wisely?
돈을 어떻게 현명하게 쓰고 모을 수 있을까요?
